If you own a large-breed dog, this is the emergency I'd most want you to recognise at 2am. Bloat, also called GDV, can kill a healthy adult dog in hours. The stomach fills with gas and twists on itself, cutting off the blood supply. The four signs to burn into memory: • A swollen, tight, distended belly • Unproductive retching and excessive drooling (trying to be sick with nothing coming up, the single most important red flag) • Restlessness, pacing, inability to settle • Collapse If any of these happen, don't wait it out. Get to an emergency vet immediately, every minute counts. High-risk breed? Feed small meals, use a slow feeder, no exercise around mealtimes, and ask your vet about gastropexy. #vetexplains #dogemergency #bloatawareness #doghealth

Living with dogs means accepting that you will quite literally never have a snack that belongs only to you. The second Bailey hears a chip bag opening, it’s basically a whistle telling her to sprint over as fast as physically possible. Suddenly, my quick little snack break turns into a full-on shareable feast because apparently everything I eat must be inspected and sampled by her too. Then I sit there wondering how she became so ridiculously spoiled like I’m not the one handing over little bites every single time. At this point, I think Bailey just lets me believe the snacks are mine until she decides she wants her share. #DogMomLife #SpoiledDog #LifeWithDogs #DogHumor #PetParents
